meta.phase-name: Schema Contract Cleanup and JSON Schema Import Path

phase-plan.purpose: Remove remaining hard-coded preset and spaces semantics from Space Explorer and Content Creator, replace TypeScript fallback schema defaults with repo schema data, and expose a neutral vector payload that can be edited and regenerated from the repo schema.
phase-plan.scope: Schema authoring surfaces, engine schema contract files, space-data generation/recompute, and test-mode import/export paths. No new gameplay systems in this slice.

file.description: Neutralize the public content-vector payload contract and remove hard-coded feature-name config from the authoring runtime config.
Rename the browser recompute surface away from trait/feature terminology and remove hard-coded combined-vector defaults.
Generate space-data.json from the repo schema document instead of hard-coded TS feature lists.
Remove TypeScript fallback schema defaults and fake semantic-axis defaults from the runtime vector model surface.
Importable top-level JSON Schema contract that now backs the repo-editable content schema document.

task.description: Remove the remaining hard-coded preset and fixed feature-name paths from Space Explorer and Content Creator state.
Audit the current JSON Schema surface and document the exact gap between the permissive content-pack stub and the required authoring contract.

Replace or wrap the current permissive content-pack schema so the app can import a real JSON Schema-backed authoring contract directly, then purge the remaining trait/semantic payload naming from generator and runtime surfaces.

decision.summary: The app must work from an importable JSON Schema-backed contract rather than a custom schema format with hard-coded semantic helpers.
decision.impact: Schema import/export becomes explicit and the authoring UI can derive structure from the same contract used by codegen.

decision.summary: Generated and browser-recomputed vector payloads must use neutral vector naming rather than trait/feature/space terminology.
decision.impact: Space Explorer reads repo-driven vector metadata without reintroducing privileged domain names into the generated content payload.
